# Adjudication Task — Chapter 267

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃267화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|파아앗!
  6|
  7|순간 플래시처럼 터진 검은 빛에 눈을 깜빡였을 뿐이다.
  8|
  9|단지 그랬을 뿐인데…….
 10|
 11|‘이 개새끼 어디 갔어.’
 12|
 13|고통도 잊힐 만큼의 충격에, 나는 멍하니 입을 벌렸다.
 14|
 15|사라졌다. 마치 지우개로 지워진 것처럼.
 16|
 17|주위에 흩뿌려진 핏물과 여전히 청풍의 목을 붙잡고 있는 혈주의 손목만이 놈이 존재했다는 유일한 증거다.
 18|
 19|띠링.
 20|
 21|
 22|
 23|- 퀘스트, [절체절명]을 성공적으로 완료했습니다!
 24|
 25|- 막대한 경험치를 얻었습니다!
 26|
 27|- 레벨 업!
 28|
 29|- 레벨 업!
 30|
 31|
 32|
 33|시스템 알림과 함께 몸 상태가 급속도로 회복되었다.
 34|
 35|부러진 뼈가 단단하게 붙고, 베이고 뭉개진 살점이 아물었다. 텅 비어 있던 단전은 가득 찼으며 근육에는 활력이 샘솟았다.
 36|
 37|하지만 단 하나, 황당함만은 사라지지 않았다.
 38|
 39|“뭐 이런 개 같은 경우가.”
 40|
 41|혈주. 무슨 수를 써서라도 그 자식만은 죽였어야 했는데.
 42|
 43|땅만 바라보며 허탈하게 중얼거리던 그때, 익숙한 목소리와 함께 손 하나가 불쑥 눈앞에 내밀어졌다.
 44|
 45|“괜찮나?”
 46|
 47|정신적으로 많이 지쳤지만, 몸은 말짱하다. 나는 종리추의 손을 붙잡고 일어났다.
 48|
 49|“어, 괜찮아. 덕분에 살았다.”
 50|
 51|“다행이군. 그럼 우선 나를 도와 부상자들을…… 한데 방금 뭐라고?”
 52|
 53|종리추가 눈을 깜빡였다.
 54|
 55|지금 무슨 소릴 들은 거지? 얼굴에 딱 그렇게 쓰여 있다.
 56|
 57|“왜?”
 58|
 59|“으, 응?”
 60|
 61|“무슨 문제 있어?”
 62|
 63|잠깐 멍한 표정으로 나를 바라보던 종리추가 손을 내저었다.
 64|
 65|“아, 아닐세. 문제는 무슨. 그런데 혹시 조금 전에…… 그거 못 들었나?”
 66|
 67|“그거? 그게 뭐야. 잠깐 기절하긴 했는데.”
 68|
 69|몸으로 때우는 것도 한계가 있더라. 맞고, 일어나고, 다시 나가떨어지고 일어나기를 수십 번도 넘게 반복하기를 한참.
 70|
 71|그러다가 어느 순간 턱을 정통으로 얻어맞고 짧게 의식이 끊겼었다.
 72|
 73|“눈 뜨니까 거의 끝나 있던데. 그 새끼 발목 보이길래 냉큼 붙잡았지.”
 74|
 75|“……그렇군.”
 76|
 77|뭔가 말할 것처럼 입을 벙긋거리던 종리추가 입을 꾹 다문다.
 78|
 79|나도 도대체 어떻게 일이 흘러갔는지, 종리추의 정체가 뭔지 묻고 싶었지만, 꾹 참았다.
 80|
 81|‘아군이라는 사실이 중요한 거지.’
 82|
 83|지금은 그걸로 충분하다. 더 급한 일이 사방에 널려 있다.
 84|
 85|“노야!”
 86|
 87|청풍도 청풍이지만, 노쇠한 적천강의 부상이 더 걱정이다.
 88|
 89|한달음에 달려가 상태를 살펴보니 가늘게 뛰는 맥박과 엷은 숨결이 느껴졌다.
 90|
 91|“잠깐 비켜 보겠나?”
 92|
 93|응급처치를 끝낸 청풍을 조심스럽게 내려놓은 종리추가 적천강의 명문혈(命門穴)에 손을 올렸다.
 94|
 95|진기가 주입되자 그의 안색이 한결 편안해지는 것이 느껴졌다.
 96|
 97|“어때?”
 98|
 99|“그리 심각한 부상은 아니야. 한 번에 너무 많은 기력을 소모해서 한동안은 의식을 차릴 수 없겠지만.”
100|
101|“청풍은?”
102|
103|“마찬가지일세. 내상이 있지만 젊으니 금방 회복하겠지.”
104|
105|“후우…….”
106|
107|“불행 중 다행이지.”
108|
109|안도의 한숨을 내쉬는 내 모습에 종리추가 빙긋 웃은 그때였다.
110|
111|쉬쉬쉬쉭!
112|
113|저 밑에서부터 빠르게 가까워지는 수많은 인기척. 그 기세가 흉흉하기 짝이 없다.
114|
115|‘설마, 또?’
116|
117|굳은 얼굴로 창대를 말아쥐는 내게 종리추가 손을 내저었다.
118|
119|“내려놓게. 아군이야.”
120|
121|그의 말은 사실이었다. 이내 모습을 드러낸 수백의 무인들의 선두에는 낯익은 얼굴들이 몇몇 끼어 있었다.
122|
123|구파일방의 누구, 오대세가의 누구.
124|
125|성라대연이 열리는 동안 상석을 지키던 이들이다.
126|
127|그러나 어쩐 일인지 벽력도왕을 포함한 핵심 인물 여럿은 보이지 않았다.
128|
129|“정지.”
130|
131|멈추지 않을 것 같던 수백 명의 발걸음이 우리 앞에서 우뚝 멈췄다.
132|
133|정지 명령을 내린 한 사람이 나와 종리추를 향해 절뚝절뚝 걸음을 옮겼다. 나뭇잎 사이로 들이친 햇빛이 강철로 만든 의족에 반사되어 반짝 빛났다.
134|
135|‘천면호리 송호.’
136|
137|나와 종리추를 훑는 그의 날카로운 눈빛에 문득 잊고 있던 사실 하나가 뇌리를 스쳤다.
138|
139|저들은 종리추가 아군이라는 사실을 모른다. 그들에게 있어 종리추는 법왕 굉도를 암살하고 소림사에 피바람을 불러일으킨 무림 공적이다.
140|
141|저벅. 저벅.
142|
143|천면호리가 의족을 내딛자 수백의 무인이 함께 움직였다.
144|
145|이거, 괜한 오해로 칼부림 나게 생겼다.
146|
147|“자, 잠깐만요. 지금 단단히 오해하고 계신 것 같은데…….”
148|
149|심상치 않은 분위기에 앞으로 나서려던 순간, 종리추가 불쑥 입을 열었다.
150|
151|“천면호리 송호.”
152|
153|“헉.”
154|
155|아니, 이 자식이 미쳤나.
156|
157|사정을 설명하고 오해를 풀어도 모자랄 판에 첫마디부터 반말을 박아 버리다니.
158|
159|“야, 야!”
160|
161|황급히 옆구리를 찔러 봤지만 이미 늦었다. 종리추의 입에서 폭탄 같은 한마디가 튀어나왔다.
162|
163|“다리는 괜찮나?”
164|
165|“……!”
166|
167|미친놈인가, 진짜.
168|
169|나도 모르게 입을 딱 벌리고 종리추를 바라봤다.
170|
171|이번에는 선을 제대로 넘었다. 반말 찍찍에 이어 장애인 비하다.
172|
173|나는 천면호리가 의족을 뽑아 종리추에게 달려들기 전에 황급히 앞으로 나섰다.
174|
175|“죄송합니다. 얘가 원래 이런 놈이 아닌데. 그냥 제가 설명할게요. 그러니까 이게 어떻게 된 일이냐면요.”
176|
177|“응? 그냥 내가 설명해도 되는데.”
178|
179|“설명은 시벌, 이 상황에 네가 뭘 설명해. 사과부터 해. 이 자식아.”
180|
181|생명의 은인이고 나발이고.
182|
183|일이 커지기 전에 종리추의 뒷목을 잡고 냅다 고개부터 숙였다.
184|
185|고개를 들자 귀신을 본 것처럼 딱딱하게 굳어 있는 천면호리의 얼굴이 보였다.
186|
187|‘화 많이 났구나.’
188|
189|하긴 이 상황에서 화가 안 나면 그게 사람이냐. 예수 아니면 부처지.
190|
191|그러나 수습을 위해 팽팽 돌아가던 사고는 다음 순간 들려온 천면호리의 대답에 우뚝 정지했다.
192|
193|“오랜만에 뵙습니다.”
194|
195|종리추가 노인네처럼 허허 웃으며 고개를 끄덕였다.
196|
197|“잘 지내는 모습을 보니 좋군. 자네가 가장 먼저 알아차릴 것 같았지.”
198|
199|“한참 헤맸습니다. 두 시진 전까지만 해도 혈귀검마(血鬼劍魔), 그 빌어먹을 놈이 반로환동을 한 줄 알았지요.”
200|
201|“저런, 자네도 늙었군.”
202|
203|“이렇게나마 늙을 수 있었던 것도 대협 덕분입니다. 그때 구해 주시지 않았다면 이 자리에 없었을 테니 말입니다.”
204|
205|의족을 톡톡 두드리며 웃던 천면호리가 말을 이었다.
206|
207|“두 시진 전 암중살(暗中殺)을 발견했습니다. 짓궂은 장난을 치셨더군요.”
208|
209|“아, 그 친구. 그러고 보니 슬슬 깨어났을 때가 됐군.”
210|
211|“응당 죽었어야 할 놈이 살아 있더군요. 그제야 헛다리 짚었다는 걸 알았습니다.”
212|
213|“들키기 싫었으니까. 성라대연이 끝날 때까지만이라도 숨기고 싶었네.”
214|
215|종리추가 씁쓸한 얼굴로 덧붙였다.
216|
217|“이런 일이 벌어질 거라고는 생각지도 못했지만.”
218|
219|“저도 같은 마음입니다. 그토록 방비했건만, 다른 곳도 아닌 소림에서 혈겁이 벌어지다니…….”
220|
221|“자네가 나타난 걸 보니 소림의 일은 정리됐겠군. 벽력도왕이 갔나?”
222|
223|“예, 상황을 파악한 즉시 인원을 나누어 두 갈래 길로 이동했습니다. 지금쯤 팽 대협께서 소림을 정리 중이실 겁니다.”
224|
225|“피해가 너무 크네. 있어서는 안 되는 일이 벌어졌어.”
226|
227|“그에 관해 드릴 말씀이 많습니다.”
228|
229|“나 역시.”
230|
231|잠깐 무거운 침묵이 흘렀다.
232|
233|반쯤 넋을 놓은 채 두 사람의 대화를 듣고 있던 나는 간신히 입을 뗐다.
234|
235|“야, 아니. 저기요.”
236|
237|종리추, 아니 ‘그’가 눈을 깜빡였다.
238|
239|“나 말인가?”
240|
241|“네. 그, 제가 뭐 좀 여쭤볼 게 있는데…….”
242|
243|“뭐든 물어보게.”
244|
245|수백 쌍의 눈빛이 얼굴을 향해 쏟아졌다. 다들 저 미친놈이 드디어 정신을 차렸구나 하는 얼굴이다.
246|
247|“혹시, 존함이?”
248|
249|시원시원한 대답이 돌아왔다.
250|
251|“매종학일세.”
252|
253|“……아하. 매종학이요.”
254|
255|전신의 솜털이 쭈뼛 섰다.
256|
257|첫 만남부터 지금까지, 그와 나눴던 대화와 내 행동들이 주마등처럼 눈앞을 스쳐 지나갔다.
258|
259|“우연인 것 같은데, 제가 아는 어떤 분이랑 이름이 같으시네요.”
260|
261|“그런가?”
262|
263|크게 심호흡했다. 심장 박동 소리가 천둥처럼 울려 퍼진다.
264|
265|‘싸늘하다.’
266|
267|가슴에 비수가 날아와 꽂힌다. 하지만 걱정하지 마라. 세상에는 동명이인들이 생각보다 많으니까.
268|
269|어쩌면 짭종학일 수도 있다. 나는 마지막 희망을 붙잡고 입을 열었다.
270|
271|“혹시 별호가……?”
272|
273|“검성.”
274|
275|“아, 네.”
276|
277|시벌, 찐이네.
278|
279|눈앞이 깜깜해진 내 귓가로 웃음기 어린 목소리가 파고들었다.
280|
281|“앞으로도 친하게 지내세. 친구.”
282|
283|“…….”
284|
285|아, 죽고 싶다.
286|
287|
288|
289|* * *
290|
291|
292|
293|깊이도, 위치도 짐작되지 않는 어느 거대한 동공.
294|
295|누구도 의미를 짐작할 수 없는 복잡한 문양과 문자가 새겨진 동공의 중심부에서 검은 광채가 뿜어져 나왔다.
296|
297|화아아악!
298|
299|거세게 타오르던 횃불마저 희미해질 정도로 깊은 어둠이 기지개를 켰다.
300|
301|잠시 후 칠흑 같은 어둠이 사라지자, 중심부를 둘러싸고 있던 수십의 흑의인들 사이로 동요가 퍼져 나갔다.
302|
303|“혈주!”
304|
305|“이게 무슨……!”
306|
307|그들의 시선이 향한 곳에는 피를 흘리며 비틀거리는 한 사람이 있었다.
308|
309|피 칠갑을 한 채 거친 숨을 몰아쉬는 청년.
310|
311|혈주의 전신에는 검상이 빼곡했고 잘려나간 두 팔의 단면에서는 쉴 새 없이 핏물이 솟구치고 있었다.
312|
313|“술사! 술사를 불러와라!”
314|
315|“혈주께서 중상을 입으셨다!”
316|
317|동공에 울려 퍼지는 다급한 외침을 들으며 혈주는 천천히 입을 벌렸다.
318|
319|마지막까지 놓치지 않았던 자신의 팔이 바닥에 털썩 떨어졌다. 주인의 몸에서 떨어져 나간 그 손아귀에는 짧은 길이의 지팡이 하나가 들려 있었다.
320|
321|어둠 속에서도 희미한 녹색 빛을 뿌리는 그 모습에 누군가가 작은 탄성을 내질렀다.
322|
323|“녹옥불장……!”
324|
325|다름 아닌 천년 소림의 신물이다.
326|
327|그 누구도 성공을 장담할 수 없었던 임무. 그러나 비록 비참한 꼴이 되었을지언정, 자신들의 상관은 임무를 훌륭히 완수했다.
328|
329|과연 ‘그분’이 아끼는 제자답게.
330|
331|“경하드립니다!”
332|
333|“경하?”
334|

“It’s good to see you doing well. I thought you would be the first to recognize me.”

[P95]
“It took me quite some time. Until two shichen[^1] ago, I thought the Blood Ghost Sword Demon—that damned bastard—had Returned to Youth.”

[P96]
“My, my. You’ve grown old too.”

[P97]
“I owe the fact that I lived long enough to grow this old to you, Great Hero. If you hadn’t saved me back then, I wouldn’t be standing here now.”

[P98]
The Thousand-Faced Fox laughed and tapped his prosthetic leg.

[P99]
“I found the Shadow Killer two shichen ago. You played quite the cruel prank.”

[P100]
“Ah, that fellow. Come to think of it, he should be waking up around now.”

[P101]
“A man who should have been dead was still alive. That was when I realized I had guessed wrong.”

[P102]
“I didn’t want anyone to find out. I wanted to keep it hidden until the Star-Array Grand Banquet ended, at least.”

[P103]
Jongni Chu’s expression turned bitter.

[P104]
“I never imagined something like this would happen.”

[P105]
“I feel the same. Despite all our precautions, a bloodbath occurred at Shaolin of all places…”

[P106]
“You wouldn’t be here unless the situation at Shaolin had been settled. Did the Thunderbolt Saber King go?”

[P107]
“Yes. As soon as we grasped the situation, we divided our forces and took two separate routes. Great Hero Peng should be handling matters at Shaolin by now.”

[P108]
“The losses are too great. Something that should never have happened has happened.”

[P109]
“I have much to tell you about that.”

[P110]
“As do I.”

[P111]
A heavy silence settled over us.

[P112]
I had been listening to their conversation in a daze, but I finally managed to speak.

[P113]
“Hey—no. Excuse me.”

[P114]
Jongni Chu—or rather, *he*—blinked.

[P115]
“Are you speaking to me?”

[P116]
“Yes. Um, there’s something I’d like to ask…”

[P117]
“Ask me anything.”

[P118]
Hundreds of pairs of eyes turned toward me. Everyone wore the same expression.

[P119]
*That lunatic has finally come to his senses.*

[P120]
“May I ask your name?”

[P121]
The answer came without hesitation.

[P122]
“Mae Jonghak.”

[P123]
“…Ah. Mae Jonghak.”

[P124]
Every hair on my body stood on end.

[P125]
From our first meeting until now, every conversation we’d had and everything I’d done flashed before my eyes.

[P126]
“What a coincidence. You have the same name as someone I know.”

[P127]
“Is that so?”

[P128]
I drew a deep breath. My heartbeat thundered in my ears.

[P129]
*It’s cold.*

[P130]
A dagger had flown straight into my chest. But there was no need to worry. More people shared the same name than you might think.

[P131]
Maybe he was Fake Jonghak.

[P132]
Clinging to that final hope, I opened my mouth.

[P133]
“Do you happen to have an epithet…?”

[P134]
“The Sword Saint.”

[P135]
“Ah. Right.”

[P136]
*Fuck. He’s the real thing.*

[P137]
As darkness swallowed my vision, an amused voice slipped into my ear.

[P138]
“Let’s remain good friends from now on. Friend.”

[P139]
“…”

[P140]
*I want to die.*

[P141]
* * *

[P142]
An enormous cavern of unknown depth in an unknown location.

[P143]
Complex patterns and characters that no one could decipher had been carved into the cavern’s center. From among them, black radiance erupted.

[P144]
*Fwoom!*

[P145]
A darkness so deep that even the fiercely burning torches dimmed stretched awake.

[P146]
When the pitch-black darkness vanished a moment later, unrest spread among the dozens of black-clad figures surrounding the cavern’s center.

[P147]
“The Blood Lord!”

[P148]
“What happened…?”

[P149]
Their gazes converged on a staggering, bleeding figure.

[P150]
A young man drenched in blood and breathing heavily.

[P151]
Sword wounds covered the Blood Lord’s body, and blood gushed ceaselessly from the severed stumps of both arms.

[P152]
“Call the sorcerers! Bring them here!”

[P153]
“The Blood Lord is gravely wounded!”

[P154]
As the urgent shouts echoed through the cavern, the Blood Lord slowly opened his mouth.

[P155]
The severed arm he had refused to let go of until the very end fell from his mouth and thudded to the floor. Its hand still clutched a short staff.

[P156]
The staff gave off a faint green light even in the darkness, drawing a quiet gasp from someone nearby.

[P157]
“The Green Jade Buddha Staff…!”

[P158]
It was none other than the sacred treasure of thousand-year-old Shaolin.

[P159]
No one had been able to guarantee the mission’s success. Yet despite the wretched state he had returned in, their superior had completed it splendidly.

[P160]
Just as expected of the Disciple cherished by *that person*.

[P161]
“Congratulations!”

[P162]
“Congratulations?”

[P163]
A red glow filled the Blood Lord’s eyes as he stared at the subordinate bowing deeply with a fist-and-palm salute.

[P164]
*Whoosh—crack!*

[P165]
The subordinate’s chest shattered, and he slammed into the wall amid a fountain of blood.

[P166]
His body trembled with a wheezing sound, then went still. There was no need to check. He was dead.

[P167]
“Throw that bastard to the beasts.”

[P168]
The instant the Blood Lord’s frigid voice left his lips, another subordinate hoisted the corpse over his shoulder and disappeared.

[P169]
This was hardly the first or second time such a thing had happened. They were merely reminded once more of how terrifying their superior was. Not one of them mourned or showed any agitation over the death of the ignorant newcomer who had stepped forward.

[P170]
“Blood Lord, you must receive treatment first…”

[P171]
“I’m dizzy. Begin.”

[P172]
The Blood Lord surrendered himself to the sorcerers who had just arrived.

[P173]
He wanted to slaughter everything in sight, but barely managed to suppress his murderous impulse.

[P174]
He needed to conserve his strength. He had to recover as quickly as possible so he could tear those bastards apart.

[P175]
*The Sword Saint. The Fire King. Cheongpung. And…*

[P176]
*The Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi, Jin Taekyung.*

[P177]
The memory of that bastard grinning through blood-soaked teeth made his blood boil.

[P178]
Unable to contain his rage, he smashed a fist into a sorcerer’s head.

[P179]
*Boom. Thud.*

[P180]
The headless body collapsed like a rotten old tree. Feeling the frightened gazes of the remaining sorcerers, the Blood Lord spat through clenched teeth,

[P181]
“I can’t afford to kill any more valuable sorcerers. Continue.”

[P182]
The treatment resumed after its brief interruption. It was a bizarre sight that defied explanation. Broken bones knitted together, and flesh grew back.

[P183]
The Blood Lord clenched his teeth against the pain that accompanied the recovery. As his vision began to turn white, one man’s face appeared before him.

[P184]
*You… I’ll kill you with my own hands. I swear.*

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

“I didn’t want anyone to find out. I wanted to keep it hidden until the Star-Array Grand Banquet ended, at least.”

[P103]
Jongni Chu’s expression turned bitter.

[P104]
“I never imagined something like this would happen.”

[P105]
“I feel the same. Despite all our precautions, a bloodbath occurred at Shaolin of all places…”

[P106]
“You wouldn’t be here unless the situation at Shaolin had been settled. Did the Thunderbolt Saber King go?”

[P107]
“Yes. As soon as we grasped the situation, we divided our forces and took two separate routes. Great Hero Peng should be handling matters at Shaolin by now.”

[P108]
“The losses are too great. Something that should never have happened has happened.”

[P109]
“I have much to tell you about that.”

[P110]
“As do I.”

[P111]
A heavy silence settled over us.

[P112]
I had been listening to their conversation in a daze, but I finally managed to speak.

[P113]
“Hey—no. Excuse me.”

[P114]
Jongni Chu—or rather, *he*—blinked.

[P115]
“Are you speaking to me?”

[P116]
“Yes. Um, there’s something I’d like to ask…”

[P117]
“Ask me anything.”

[P118]
Hundreds of pairs of eyes turned toward me. Everyone wore the same expression.

[P119]
*That lunatic has finally come to his senses.*

[P120]
“May I ask your name?”

[P121]
The answer came without hesitation.

[P122]
“Mae Jonghak.”

[P123]
“…Ah. Mae Jonghak.”

[P124]
Every hair on my body stood on end.

[P125]
From our first meeting until now, every conversation we’d had and everything I’d done flashed before my eyes.

[P126]
“What a coincidence. You have the same name as someone I know.”

[P127]
“Is that so?”

[P128]
I drew a deep breath. My heartbeat thundered in my ears.

[P129]
*It’s cold.*

[P130]
A dagger had flown straight into my chest. But there was no need to worry. More people shared the same name than you might think.

[P131]
Maybe he was Fake Jonghak.

[P132]
Clinging to that final hope, I opened my mouth.

[P133]
“Do you happen to have an epithet…?”

[P134]
“The Sword Saint.”

[P135]
“Ah. Right.”

[P136]
*Fuck. He’s the real thing.*

[P137]
As darkness swallowed my vision, an amused voice slipped into my ear.

[P138]
“Let’s remain good friends from now on. Friend.”

[P139]
“…”

[P140]
*I want to die.*

[P141]
* * *

[P142]
An enormous cavern of unknown depth in an unknown location.

[P143]
Complex patterns and characters that no one could decipher had been carved into the cavern’s center. From among them, black radiance erupted.

[P144]
*Fwoom!*

[P145]
A darkness so deep that even the fiercely burning torches dimmed stretched awake.

[P146]
When the pitch-black darkness vanished a moment later, unrest spread among the dozens of black-clad figures surrounding the cavern’s center.

[P147]
“The Blood Lord!”

[P148]
“What happened…?”

[P149]
Their gazes converged on a staggering, bleeding figure.

[P150]
A young man drenched in blood and breathing heavily.

[P151]
Sword wounds covered the Blood Lord’s body, and blood gushed ceaselessly from the severed stumps of both arms.

[P152]
“Call the sorcerers! Bring them here!”

[P153]
“The Blood Lord is gravely wounded!”

[P154]
As the urgent shouts echoed through the cavern, the Blood Lord slowly opened his mouth.

[P155]
The severed arm he had refused to let go of until the very end fell from his mouth and thudded to the floor. Its hand still clutched a short staff.

[P156]
The staff gave off a faint green light even in the darkness, drawing a quiet gasp from someone nearby.

[P157]
“The Green Jade Buddha Staff…!”

[P158]
It was none other than the sacred treasure of thousand-year-old Shaolin.

[P159]
No one had been able to guarantee the mission’s success. Yet despite the wretched state he had returned in, their superior had completed it splendidly.

[P160]
Just as expected of the Disciple cherished by *that person*.

[P161]
“Congratulations!”

[P162]
“Congratulations?”

[P163]
A red glow filled the Blood Lord’s eyes as he stared at the subordinate bowing deeply with a fist-and-palm salute.

[P164]
*Whoosh—crack!*

[P165]
The subordinate’s chest shattered, and he slammed into the wall amid a fountain of blood.

[P166]
His body trembled with a wheezing sound, then went still. There was no need to check. He was dead.

[P167]
“Throw that bastard to the beasts.”

[P168]
The instant the Blood Lord’s frigid voice left his lips, another subordinate hoisted the corpse over his shoulder and disappeared.

[P169]
This was hardly the first or second time such a thing had happened. They were merely reminded once more of how terrifying their superior was. Not one of them mourned or showed any agitation over the death of the ignorant newcomer who had stepped forward.

[P170]
“Blood Lord, you must receive treatment first…”

[P171]
“I’m dizzy. Begin.”

[P172]
The Blood Lord surrendered himself to the sorcerers who had just arrived.

[P173]
He wanted to slaughter everything in sight, but barely managed to suppress his murderous impulse.

[P174]
He needed to conserve his strength. He had to recover as quickly as possible so he could tear those bastards apart.

[P175]
*The Sword Saint. The Fire King. Cheongpung. And…*

[P176]
*The Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi, Jin Taekyung.*

[P177]
The memory of that bastard grinning through blood-soaked teeth made his blood boil.

[P178]
Unable to contain his rage, he smashed a fist into a sorcerer’s head.

[P179]
*Boom. Thud.*

[P180]
The headless body collapsed like a rotten old tree. Feeling the frightened gazes of the remaining sorcerers, the Blood Lord spat through clenched teeth,

[P181]
“I can’t afford to kill any more valuable sorcerers. Continue.”

[P182]
The treatment resumed after its brief interruption. It was a bizarre sight that defied explanation. Broken bones knitted together, and flesh grew back.

[P183]
The Blood Lord clenched his teeth against the pain that accompanied the recovery. As his vision began to turn white, one man’s face appeared before him.

[P184]
*You… I’ll kill you with my own hands. I swear.*

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

```text
  1|＃267화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|파아앗!
  6|
  7|순간 플래시처럼 터진 검은 빛에 눈을 깜빡였을 뿐이다.
  8|
  9|단지 그랬을 뿐인데…….
 10|
 11|‘이 개새끼 어디 갔어.’
 12|
 13|고통도 잊힐 만큼의 충격에, 나는 멍하니 입을 벌렸다.
 14|
 15|사라졌다. 마치 지우개로 지워진 것처럼.
 16|
 17|주위에 흩뿌려진 핏물과 여전히 청풍의 목을 붙잡고 있는 혈주의 손목만이 놈이 존재했다는 유일한 증거다.
 18|
 19|띠링.
 20|
 21|
 22|
 23|- 퀘스트, [절체절명]을 성공적으로 완료했습니다!
 24|
 25|- 막대한 경험치를 얻었습니다!
 26|
 27|- 레벨 업!
 28|
 29|- 레벨 업!
 30|
 31|
 32|
 33|시스템 알림과 함께 몸 상태가 급속도로 회복되었다.
 34|
 35|부러진 뼈가 단단하게 붙고, 베이고 뭉개진 살점이 아물었다. 텅 비어 있던 단전은 가득 찼으며 근육에는 활력이 샘솟았다.
 36|
 37|하지만 단 하나, 황당함만은 사라지지 않았다.
 38|
 39|“뭐 이런 개 같은 경우가.”
 40|
 41|혈주. 무슨 수를 써서라도 그 자식만은 죽였어야 했는데.
 42|
 43|땅만 바라보며 허탈하게 중얼거리던 그때, 익숙한 목소리와 함께 손 하나가 불쑥 눈앞에 내밀어졌다.
 44|
 45|“괜찮나?”
 46|
 47|정신적으로 많이 지쳤지만, 몸은 말짱하다. 나는 종리추의 손을 붙잡고 일어났다.
 48|
 49|“어, 괜찮아. 덕분에 살았다.”
 50|
 51|“다행이군. 그럼 우선 나를 도와 부상자들을…… 한데 방금 뭐라고?”
 52|
 53|종리추가 눈을 깜빡였다.
 54|
 55|지금 무슨 소릴 들은 거지? 얼굴에 딱 그렇게 쓰여 있다.
 56|
 57|“왜?”
 58|
 59|“으, 응?”
 60|
 61|“무슨 문제 있어?”
 62|
 63|잠깐 멍한 표정으로 나를 바라보던 종리추가 손을 내저었다.
 64|
 65|“아, 아닐세. 문제는 무슨. 그런데 혹시 조금 전에…… 그거 못 들었나?”
 66|
 67|“그거? 그게 뭐야. 잠깐 기절하긴 했는데.”
 68|
 69|몸으로 때우는 것도 한계가 있더라. 맞고, 일어나고, 다시 나가떨어지고 일어나기를 수십 번도 넘게 반복하기를 한참.
 70|
 71|그러다가 어느 순간 턱을 정통으로 얻어맞고 짧게 의식이 끊겼었다.
 72|
 73|“눈 뜨니까 거의 끝나 있던데. 그 새끼 발목 보이길래 냉큼 붙잡았지.”
 74|
 75|“……그렇군.”
 76|
 77|뭔가 말할 것처럼 입을 벙긋거리던 종리추가 입을 꾹 다문다.
 78|
 79|나도 도대체 어떻게 일이 흘러갔는지, 종리추의 정체가 뭔지 묻고 싶었지만, 꾹 참았다.
 80|
 81|‘아군이라는 사실이 중요한 거지.’
 82|
 83|지금은 그걸로 충분하다. 더 급한 일이 사방에 널려 있다.
 84|
 85|“노야!”
 86|

## Adjudicator rules

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.
